extracted.intended_audience: general readers and film/awards followers seeking a summary of the 79th BAFTA Film Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Encyclopedic coverage and documentation of the 79th British Academy Film Awards (BAFTAs), including eligibility note, longlist/nominations timeline, full list of categories, winners and nominees, ceremony details, controversies, and aftermath. Intended as a record of the event and its outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: films screened at British cinemas in 2025
rubrics_metrics.description: Accolades were given for the best feature-length films and documentaries of any nationality that were screened at British cinemas in 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the eligibility condition stated for the films considered for the 79th BAFTAs; it specifies timeframe (films screened in 2025) and venue requirement (British cinemas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Winners formatting guideline (article)
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are listed first and highlighted in boldface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longlist / nominations / winners timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: BAFTA longlists were announced on 9 January 2026; nominations were announced on 27 January 2026; winners were announced on 22 February 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline and procedural milestones for the awards process as documented in the article; indicates sequence for selection and public announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistics: multiple nominations and awards as metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The article tracks films that received multiple nominations and films that received multiple awards (e.g., One Battle After Another received 14 nominations and 6 awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counting nominations and awards is presented as a way to measure relative success and prominence at the ceremony; the article provides a summary table of these statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: BBC broadcast editing and timing practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC edited the three-hour ceremony into a two-hour broadcast window; acceptance speeches were edited and there was a two-hour delay between the live event and the broadcast, ordinarily used to remove problematic material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes broadcaster practices (time-limited edit, tape delay for content removal) and how those practices were applied (and criticized) in this ceremony; context for controversies about content that remained in the broadcast.

rubrics_metrics.name: BAFTA / event inclusion practice re: attendee with Tourette's
rubrics_metrics.description: BAFTA announced to the audience before the ceremony and throughout that John Davidson (present in the room) may make involuntary strong language, noises or movements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented inclusion/notification practice intended to prepare attendees and broadcasters for involuntary tics; cited in the article as part of the controversy and BAFTA's duty-of-care statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: BBC editorial standards and breach finding
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC's Executive Complaints Unit (ECU) found the inclusion of Davidson's outburst in the broadcast 'had no editorial justification and represented a breach of the BBC's editorial standards, but that the breach was unintentional'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarises the BBC's post-event investigation conclusion and remedial promise; indicates that airing such slurs contravenes the broadcaster's editorial rules even if unintentional.
